findings.issue: Every entry in `resources` carries a `distributions` key (with sub-keys `path`, `bytes`, `format`, `media_type`, `conforms_to`, `conforms_to_standard`). The schema digest lists no `distributions` slot on Dataset/CoreDataset, and `resources` has range `Dataset`, whose accepted slots are the top-level Dataset inventory. `distributions` is an invented key and will fail validation or be silently dropped; the file-level facts belong in `file_collections` (which declares `path`, `file_count`, `total_bytes`, `collection_type`) as they are in the full record.

The nine data-type directories, the root metadata group, and the three recommended splits are all placed in `resources` (range Dataset). In the full record these are `file_collections` (range FileCollection) and `subsets` (range DataSubset) respectively. Collapsing three distinct declared ranges into one loses the `collection_type`, `file_count`, `total_bytes`, `is_data_split` and `is_subpopulation` structure, and the slot description for `resources` explicitly directs file collections to `file_collections` instead.

`creators[0].id` is `https://aireadi.org`, a project website URL used as the identifier for the creating entity, and the same URL is repeated as `affiliations[0].id`. The declared creator in the FAIRhub DataCite record is the organization 'AI-READI Consortium'; the bundle supplies no registry identifier for it. Using a homepage URL as an organization identifier, and reusing it for both the Creator and one of its own affiliations, is a shape defect (self-affiliation) rather than a supported identifier.

Same defect as the full record: `creators[0].id` and `affiliations[0].id` are both `https://aireadi.org`, producing a Creator affiliated with itself and using a website URL where an organization identifier is required.

`funders[0].grants[*].id` is `uriorcurie`. The values are `https://reporter.nih.gov/search/...` resolver URLs. The bundle states the award numbers (OT2OD032644, 1OT2OD032644) and the FAIRhub metadata gives the award URI, but no declared prefix covers NIH RePORTER, so a URL is defensible; however the two entries are the same core award (OT2OD032644) recorded twice under different RePORTER application records, which produces two Grant identities for one grant. The source_caveat acknowledges this but the duplication is still an identity defect.
Identical duplicate-grant defect carried over from the full record: one NIH core award OT2OD032644 is represented as two Grant objects with two different RePORTER URLs.

`contact_person` is populated with Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648). The bundle names Aaron Lee as central contact and study PI for the *study*, and gives contact@aireadi.org as the study central contact email; no source names any individual as the licensing contact. The license names Washington University in St. Louis as licensor and directs users to docs.aireadi.org. This is an unsupported inference.
Same unsupported inference as the full record: Aaron Lee assigned as the license contact person with no source support.

Aaron Lee is assigned as the governance committee contact. The bundle states the BMJ protocol's Data Access Committee was still developing requirements and names no committee contact; the RO-Crate names the AI-READI Consortium as the governance committee without a contact person. Unsupported.
Same unsupported assignment of Aaron Lee as governance committee contact.

Aaron Lee assigned as Data Access Committee contact. The record's own `data_governance.source_caveats` states 'the input sources do not name the committee's members, give its contact details...'. The populated value directly contradicts the sibling caveat — an internal inconsistency.
Same internal inconsistency: `committee_contact` is populated with Aaron Lee while `source_caveats` on the same object states the sources do not give the committee's contact details.

`committee_name: AI-READI Data Access Committee`. The BMJ protocol refers to 'the Data Access Committee'; no source gives the name 'AI-READI Data Access Committee'. The RO-Crate names 'AI-READI Consortium' as `dataGovernanceCommittee`. The composed name is a mild fabrication.
Same composed committee name not attested in any source.

`credit_roles` lists six CRediT values (conceptualization, methodology, investigation, data_curation, project_administration, funding_acquisition) for the AI-READI Consortium. No source in the bundle assigns CRediT roles to the creator; the Nature Metabolism author-contribution statement says only that the Writing Committee created the first draft. These are inferred rather than evidenced.
Same six unevidenced CRediT `credit_roles` carried into the core record.

`confidentiality_level: restricted`. The only confidentiality statement in the bundle is the RO-Crate's `HL7:2N (normal)`. The record's own `notes` concede the enum value reflects the agent's reading of the access process rather than the source value. Mapping 'normal' to 'restricted' is an interpretive leap not supported by the evidence; 'unrestricted' would be the closer reading of HL7:2N.
Same interpretive mapping of HL7:2N (normal) to the enum value `restricted`.

`data_use_permission: disease_specific_research`. Supportable for the public set (T2DM-only attestation), but the same license simultaneously grants use 'for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes' and the DataCite consent record sets consentNoncommercial=false and consentResearchType=false. A single enum value cannot represent both; the choice is defensible but the conflict is not flagged in a caveat.
Same unflagged tension between `disease_specific_research` and the license's explicit grant of commercial and general research use.

`data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43` (Diabetes) is populated but `data_substrate` is omitted, despite the dataset being overwhelmingly composed of substrates the B2AI_SUBSTRATE enumeration covers directly (11=DICOM, 41=Tab-separated values, 6=CSV, 20=JSON, 49=Waveform Data, 69=Time-series data). A single Instance cannot carry the list, but the omission of any substrate term where several fit is a supported-but-unpopulated slot.
Same omission of `data_substrate` where the enumeration supplies fitting terms.

The full record populates `relationships` (Relationships range) with the statement that all instances belong to one prospective project and are linked by participant ID. The core record drops the slot and folds the content into `instances[0].notes`. `relationships` is a declared CoreDataset slot per the shared inventory; moving structured content into a prose note is a downgrade, and the core now states in `notes` what the full record states in a structured slot.

The core `notes` states participant compensation ('Participants received a 200 USD stipend... together with reimbursement of reasonable parking, transit or rideshare costs'). The full record carries this in the structured `participant_compensation` slot (HumanSubjectCompensation). The core omits `participant_compensation` entirely and restates its content as prose in `notes`, contrary to the instruction that notes hold only residual content after every fitting slot is used.

The core `notes` states the recommended split proportions and counts ('1,576 participants to training, 352 to validation and 352 to test, in 70/15/15 proportions'). The full record carries this in the structured `splits` slot. The core omits `splits` and restates it as prose.

The full record populates `participant_privacy` with anonymization_method, privacy_techniques, reidentification_risk and data_linkage. The core omits the slot and folds part of its content (watermarking, verified-ID login, residual re-identification risk) into `is_deidentified.deidentification_details`. `participant_privacy` is a declared slot in the shared inventory; the fold-in loses `reidentification_risk` and `data_linkage` as addressable fields.

Four Collection/Ethics-module slots populated in the full record are omitted from the core without their content being carried anywhere: `collection_consents`, `collection_notifications`, `consent_revocations`, and `direct_collection`. Partial content survives only inside `informed_consent.consent_documentation` and `informed_consent.withdrawal_mechanism`; the notification pathway (mailed letter, personalized email, REDCap interface, phone alternative) and the direct-vs-EHR-screening distinction are lost entirely.

The core populates `labeling_strategies` with a statement that no labeling was performed. The full record does not populate this slot. This is core content the full record does not state — a phase-4 direction violation — although the underlying fact is supported by the bundle and appears in the full record's `instances[0].label_description`.

The core populates `use_repository` with a statement that no such repository exists, pointing `repository_url` at the documentation site. The full record does not populate this slot. Core states content the full record does not; additionally, a slot whose purpose is to name use-tracking repositories is being used to record that none exists, which per the guidance should be an omission.

The core populates `extension_mechanism` with 'there is currently no mechanism for others to extend or augment the dataset' and supplies `contribution_url: https://aireadi.org/contact`. The full record does not populate this slot. Core states content the full record does not, and the `contribution_url` asserts a contribution pathway that the same object's text denies exists — internally inconsistent and unsupported (the bundle gives that URL as a general contact page, not a contribution route).

The core adds `versions_available: [1.0.0, 2.0.0, 3.0.0]`, a field the full record's `version_access` object does not populate. Supported by the bundle, but it is core content absent from the full record.

All minted fragment identifiers (e.g. `doi:10.60775/fairhub.3#train`, `doi:10.60775/fairhub.3#cardiac_ecg`) are appended to the dataset DOI in `doi:` CURIE form. A DOI does not admit fragments as a resolvable construct, so these CURIEs will not resolve; the practice is defensible as a traceable label but the resulting identifiers are non-resolvable, and the same fragments recur in the core record's `resources[*].id` where the range is Dataset rather than FileCollection/DataSubset.

`publisher` has range `uriorcurie` and is populated with `https://fairhub.io/`. The bundle names the publisher as 'FAIRhub' (DataCite publisherName). A bare homepage URL as publisher identifier is weak but no declared prefix covers FAIRhub, so this is tolerable; noting for completeness that the same value doubles as the platform URL elsewhere in the record.
Same use of `https://fairhub.io/` as the publisher identifier.

`external_resources[2].external_resources` holds two URLs joined by ' and ' in a single string ('https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi and https://github.com/AI-READI'). These are two distinct external resources; the multivalued-entity rule requires one object per distinct entity, or at minimum one value per URL.
Same two-URLs-in-one-string defect carried over.

The third entry gives `start_date: 2023-07-19` and `end_date: 2026-11-30` for the 'planned overall recruitment window'. The 2026-11-30 date is the protocol's stated recruitment end; the FAIRhub study record gives an anticipated completion of 2027-01-01. Mixing a FAIRhub start date with a BMJ end date composes a window no single source states. The caveat mentions both dates but the composed range is still synthetic.
Same synthetic composed recruitment window (2023-07-19 to 2026-11-30) blending FAIRhub and BMJ values.

The list includes `RO_CRATE` at dataset level on the strength of the bundled RO-Crate metadata file. The RO-Crate describes the dataset rather than being a format the dataset's own content follows; the dataset's CDS metadata file list does not include ro-crate-metadata.json. Arguably an over-claim, though the RO-Crate does declare `conformsTo` RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT for the crate itself.
Same RO_CRATE inclusion at dataset level.

British spellings appear in prose the record composes rather than quotes: 'totalling', 'generalisability', 'prioritisation', 'organised'/'harmonised' variants, 'behaviour', 'centred', 'colour', 'metres', 'centimetre'. The instruction requires American English for record prose. Some of these ('harmonised', 'colour fundus') trace to quoted source wording, but 'totalling', 'generalisability' and 'prioritisation' occur in agent-composed sentences.
Same British spellings carried into the core record's composed prose.

The `citation` value composes a DataCite-style citation ('AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset... FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'). This exact string appears in the RO-Crate `associatedPublication` list, so it is attested; noting only that the license and documentation both direct users to docs.aireadi.org for the current citation rather than supplying a fixed string, which the value does not mention.
The core omits `citation` entirely although the full record populates it and the slot exists in the shared inventory. This is a supported omission of a declared, evidenced slot.

The core omits `total_file_count` (356343) and `total_size_bytes` (3815969779678), both of which the full record carries and both of which the bundle states directly in the FAIRhub API record. These are declared slots in the shared inventory; their omission from the core loses top-level scale facts that are then only recoverable by summing the `resources[*].distributions[*].bytes` values.

`variables[1].variable_name: recommended_split` with `categories: [train; val; test]`. The categories value is a single semicolon-delimited string rather than three list entries; the same pattern recurs across `diabetes_status_group`, `sex`, `race_ethnicity`, and `monofilament_response`. Where `categories` is multivalued, one value per category is required.

`variables[*].missing_value_code` on `continuous_glucose` holds a prose explanation of why gaps arise ('Gaps arise where the sensor failed...') rather than a missing-value code. The field asks for the code used to represent missingness; the content belongs in `quality_notes` or `notes`.

`notes` states the FAIRhub view count (24,636) and citation count (zero) as of capture. These are volatile platform statistics rather than dataset facts; supported by the bundle but of low durability, and the same figures are repeated in the core `notes`.

Set to `false`. The FAIRhub DataCite record sets `deIdentDirect: true` and `deIdentHIPAA: true` under a `NoDeIdentification` type, and the RO-Crate sets `deidentified: true`. The `false` value is the correct reading of the released public set, but the record does not reconcile it against the DataCite `deIdentDirect: true` flag, which on a plain reading asserts direct identifiers were present and treated.
Same unreconciled `false` against the DataCite deIdentDirect flag.

summary: Both records are densely and largely faithfully grounded in the declared bundle, with strong source_caveats discipline: the ten substantive source disagreements (acronym expansion, WashU-vs-UW attribution, enrollment start date, target N, documentation carry-over text, demographic-subpopulation answer, blank healthsheet items, RO-Crate sensitive-information list, study-year labeling, upper age limit) are each identified and adjudicated against the declared ranking. The defects cluster in three areas. First, shape: the core record's `resources` slot invents a `distributions` sub-key that the schema does not declare, and collapses what the full record correctly models as `file_collections` (FileCollection) and `subsets` (DataSubset) into a single Dataset-ranged slot, losing `collection_type`, `file_count`, `total_bytes`, `is_data_split` and `is_subpopulation`; several `categories` values are semicolon-delimited strings where lists are required. Second, unsupported identity and contact assignments: `https://aireadi.org` is used as an organization identifier and as a Creator's own affiliation in both records, and Aaron Lee is assigned as license contact, governance committee contact and data access committee contact with no source support — the last of these directly contradicting the sibling `source_caveats` that says no committee contact is named. Six CRediT roles and a composed committee name are likewise inferred rather than evidenced. Third, phase-4 reconciliation drift: the core states content the full record does not (`labeling_strategies`, `use_repository`, `extension_mechanism`, `versions_available`), while omitting declared slots the full record populates and folding their content into prose `notes` (`participant_compensation`, `splits`, `relationships`, `participant_privacy`) or dropping it entirely (`collection_notifications`, `consent_revocations`, `direct_collection`, `citation`, `total_file_count`, `total_size_bytes`). Minor issues include duplicate Grant objects for one NIH award, two URLs concatenated in one `external_resources` value, a synthetic composed recruitment window, non-resolvable DOI-fragment identifiers, an interpretive HL7:2N-to-`restricted` mapping, an omitted `data_substrate` where enumeration terms fit, and residual British spellings in agent-composed prose.
